data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 demands a causal-mechanism story but never specifies the mechanism by which 'theory-quality × execution-fidelity' produces the comparative reliability verdict for the specific setup in the problem (panel of non-experts vs. single expert, verifiable outcomes). The claim that 'when the frozen theory is causally complete, the panel's adherence is the mechanism of reliability' asserts a label, not a mechanism: it does not identify the causal chain from non-expert panel execution of checklist items to more-reliable verifiable judgments, nor does it address why panel aggregation (rather than a single non-expert with the same checklist) is part of the mechanism. Without that, the proposed reliability gain could be an artifact of variance reduction rather than theory-quality, which the target never rules out.
